{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Software License and Maintenance Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side — Sparkling)
**Re:** Playbook review of the Garman Software License and Maintenance Agreement
**Status:** Findings verified against the document as supplied; verification step skipped on all items.

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook. On balance the paper is favourable to us in several respects: the licence is perpetual while fees are paid, we hold a 90-day termination-for-convenience right with no exit fee, there is no vendor audit right, no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum commitment, no MFN and no liquidated damages payable by us. The warranty package in § 12 and the Vendor IP indemnity in § 13 (uncapped by virtue of the § 15 carve-out) both meet or exceed our fallback positions.

Six items require action. Three are critical or high-severity structural gaps: (i) § 13 sweeps ownership of "all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to" the Agreement, which on its face captures our own materials, branding and the data Garman converts under § 4(b), with no statement anywhere that we retain rights in our data; (ii) § 15 contains **no monetary cap at all**, so we bear unlimited liability for direct damages; and (iii) § 20(d), read with § 3(c), is a flat consent requirement on assignment with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard. In addition, the licence is non-transferable and silent on contractors, § 19 is a full no-hire rather than a non-solicit, there is no post-termination transition assistance or data-return obligation, and there is no vendor insurance covenant.

Governing law (§ 20(h), Nova Scotia law, non-exclusive venue) sits outside our accepted list on a literal reading but runs in our favour — it is our home jurisdiction, the vendor's is Saskatchewan, and there is no arbitration or foreign seat. We flag it for business confirmation only and recommend accepting it as drafted.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Unqualified ownership sweep of "all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement" is not limited to Garman-provided items and captures our materials, branding and converted data; no statement that we retain rights in our data (§ 14 treats data only as confidential information). |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 15 Limitation of Garman's Liability | No monetary cap anywhere; each party, including us, bears unlimited liability for direct damages. Fails the fallback (mutual cap of at least 12 months' fees). Mutual consequential-damages exclusion and the §§ 13/14 carve-outs are acceptable and preserved. |
| 3 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Vendor-side IP indemnity covering Losses, settlements and legal fees, with procure/replace/modify remedies; uncapped via the § 15 carve-out, so better than the fallback 3x-fees super-cap. No Customer-side indemnity anywhere. No express "defend" duty, no refund remedy and a 10-day claim notice — noted, not flagged. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | Page 10 (§ 20(d); § 3(c)) | Flat consent requirement on assignment with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard; fails the fallback and sits in walk-away territory. No change-of-control termination or re-pricing right, so nothing to delete there. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 2 Grant of License | Affiliate coverage and perpetuity are good (better than fallback on affiliates). Fails the fallback on transferability: licence is "non-transferable", § 3(c) bars sublicence/assignment absent consent, § 20(d) has no successor carve-out; contractors acting on our behalf are unaddressed. |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 Grant of License | Licence expressly non-exclusive; no sole-supplier obligation; §§ 10–11 do not require us to take support only from Garman. Meets preferred position. |
| 7 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 17 Term and Termination | No liquidated damages, penalty, cancellation charge or early-termination fee on us; § 17(b) convenience right carries no termination payment. Refund/perpetual-licence mechanic on Garman default runs in our favour. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use | § 3 is limited to conventional licence-scope restrictions; no field-of-use or territory covenant; § 14(c) preserves independent development. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant (at fallback) | § 17 Term and Termination | Unconditional customer right on 90 days' notice, no fee; Garman has no convenience right. Sits at the fallback (60–90 days) rather than the preferred 30 days. Silence on pro-rata refund of prepaid maintenance noted only. |
| 10 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | **Deviation** | § 19 Non-Solicitation of Employees | Drafted as a no-hire covering "any employee of the other party" for the term plus one year, with no limitation to personnel involved in the services and no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-outs. No-hire provisions covering all personnel are walk-away territory. |
| 11 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | **Missing** | § 17 Term and Termination | § 17 runs one way only (we cease use and return/destroy Garman materials). No wind-down assistance, no return of our data (which Garman handles under § 4) and no certified deletion. Fails even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus 30-day export). |
| 12 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Needs review (business call)** | Page 10 (§ 20(h)) | Nova Scotia law and non-exclusive venue is outside the accepted list, but is our home jurisdiction (vendor is in Saskatchewan), with no arbitration and no foreign seat. Benefits us; we recommend acceptance absent a portfolio-consistency instruction. |
| 13 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use | No audit, inspection or verification right binding us anywhere; better than preferred. The only examination right (escrow materials) runs in our favour. We deliberately do not introduce audit language. |
| 14 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No pricing-parity or best-terms undertaking; § 11 simply requires payment per the Fee Schedule. |
| 15 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No minimum, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume cap; maintenance runs in renewable one-year terms; 90-day exit right preserved. |
| 16 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 10 Maintenance and Support | Maintenance is a "renewable one-year term" (renewal by agreement), no auto-renewal and no non-renewal notice hurdle; licence perpetual while fees are paid. No renewal reminder and no uplift cap — commercial ask only. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 12 Specifications and Warranty | Conformance warranty for the acceptance period plus one year and for so long as Maintenance Services continue; real remedies (correction, repair, full refund on rejection); no "AS IS" and no implied-warranty disclaimer. Absence of services/compliance/no-malicious-code warranties noted only. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | Page 10 (General Matters) | No insurance covenant anywhere, for a vendor that installs at Authorized Locations, converts our data and delivers on-site training. Falls below the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) and into walk-away territory. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the findings that our playbook treats as walk-away territory rather than ordinary negotiation. We should not sign as drafted without movement on each.

1. **Customer IP and data ownership (§ 13).** The unqualified ownership sweep of "all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement" is not confined to Garman-provided items and, with no retained-rights statement anywhere, leaves live the risk that our data, materials and branding pass to the Vendor.
2. **Unlimited liability (§ 15).** No cap of any kind; our own exposure for direct damages is unlimited, against a fallback requiring a mutual cap of at least 12 months' fees.
3. **Blanket assignment prohibition (§ 20(d), with § 3(c)).** Consent required for any assignment, with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard — a blanket bar on customer assignment.
4. **No-hire covenant (§ 19).** A term-plus-one-year prohibition on hiring any employee of the other party, unlimited by involvement in the services and without advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-outs.
5. **No vendor insurance.** No coverage at all for a vendor that accesses our data and attends our premises.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redlines** on the six actionable items:
   - § 13 — limit the ownership sweep to Garman-provided materials and add a Customer Data/materials ownership sentence with a no-joint-ownership confirmation, leaving Garman's ownership of its Software undisturbed.
   - § 15 — insert a mutual aggregate cap at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, with uncapped Excluded Claims (indemnities, confidentiality/data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) and confirmation that fees due are not "damages"; preserve the existing §§ 13/14 carve-out. Fallback: a straight 12 months' fees cap.
   - § 20(d) and § 3(c) — add an affiliate/successor carve-out for us on written notice, a not-unreasonably-withheld standard for other assignments, and a bar on Garman assigning to a competitor of ours; the § 3(c) edit is a conforming cross-reference.
   - § 2 — extend the licensed user group to contractors acting on our behalf and permit consent-free assignment of the licence to a successor in a merger or sale of the business.
   - § 19 — convert the no-hire into a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, running from the end of their involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.
   - New § 17(d) — six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, 30-day return of our data in machine-readable form, certified deletion thereafter; flag the 90-day fallback in the comment.
   - New § 20(k) — insurance covenant (CGL, E&O, cyber, workers' compensation) at preferred limits, certificates on request; offer the fallback limits (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) in the comment.
2. **Obtain a business decision on governing law.** Absent a specific instruction that the deal team wants a US-law contract for portfolio consistency, we recommend accepting § 20(h) as drafted. If instructed otherwise, the minimal edit is to substitute New York law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, leaving the rest of § 20(h) intact.
3. **Two commercial asks (not legal redlines).** Confirm with procurement whether the Fee Schedule permits Garman to reset maintenance fees on renewal; if so, request a CPI/3% uplift cap. Separately, consider asking for a pro-rata refund of prepaid maintenance on a convenience termination, which § 17 does not address.
4. **Drafting nits to raise only if the document is otherwise reopening.** Clarify "renewable" in § 10 as "renewable by mutual written agreement"; consider adding an express duty to "defend" and a refund remedy in § 13, and services/compliance-with-laws/no-malicious-code warranties in § 12. None of these defeats a fallback and none is being redlined.
5. **Do not introduce** audit language into the Agreement. Garman currently has no audit right at all, and inserting a limited one would create a vendor entitlement we do not presently face."}
